endorsements.quote: Before adopting an AI diagnostic tool, healthcare institutions should require provider-side evidence concerning dataset representativeness, subgroup performance, documentation, and foreseeable bias risks.
Procurement should therefore pause or restrict deployment until adequate real-world geriatric data are collected.

Effective implementation therefore requires clear contractual demarcation, named audit ownership, incident-escalation rules, and integration with hospital patient-safety committees to support the resolution of accountability disputes.

Continuous post-market surveillance is intended to support accessibility, detect emerging subgroup disparities, and enable administrative and public oversight, but its effectiveness depends on institutional capacity and enforcement [ 25 ].

During active clinical use, multidisciplinary teams including experts in medicine, gerontology, sociology, ethics, and law govern threshold calibration, periodic audits, and escalated non-acute cases [ 21 ].
Clinicians remain bound by the professional standard of care and independent clinical judgment.

unlisted_practices: Involve older adults in CDSS development, usability testing, and local calibration of bias sensitivity thresholds through participatory design.
Require vendors to use or evaluate federated learning methodologies during pre-market development where appropriate.
Implement a deterministic hardcoded safety mode that suppresses or quarantines age-dominant AI outputs during acute or high-load conditions while preserving attending-clinician authority.
Define and locally calibrate a bias sensitivity threshold on the normalized age-attribution ratio to trigger multidisciplinary escalation of AI outputs.
Do not use synthetic data to conceal an absence of representative source data.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual governance framework paper proposing theoretical protocols (e.g., Targeted Escalation Protocol, Autonomous High-Load Safety Mode) and illustrating them via an ICU thought experiment rather than an empirical evaluation.
